To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
private companies that hire Big 4 audited experience a dollar value increase in enterprise value due not hiring a Big-4 auditor ranging from 2.0 million to 5.2 million.
private company targets that hire Big 4 audited receive higher sale proceeds.
private companies that hire a Big 4 audit firm receive higher sale proceeds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel and potentially significant effect of the Big 4 auditor selection decision on the proceeds of private company sales.
the information value of hiring a Big 5 auditor for a private company, and the results suggest that the Big 5 audit premium may be larger for private companies than for public ones.
a new dimension of the PCD, one related to information quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Big 4 audit quality is associated with higher sale proceeds, but that the magnitude of the effect is small.
private firms hiring Big 4 audited financial statements receive higher sale proceeds, but that this effect does not fully offset the PCD.
private company targets that hire a Big 4 firm receive higher proceeds, but the precise mechanism is still unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Big 4 auditor selection is an important factor in the PCD.
private company sellers that hire Big 4 audited firms experience a substantial increase in sale proceeds, and that this effect is robust to the sale structure.
private firms that hire a Big 4 audit firm receive higher sale proceeds, which may be due to a combination of higher audit quality and lower income-increasing accrivals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PCD may be larger than previously thought.
the Big 4 auditor's role is more than just providing a signal of quality to the buyer.
the PCD is not a monolithic phenomenon, and that there are important differences between private company sales structured with stock and those structured as asset purchases.
